chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Maraghi reported to me, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, from his father (peace be upon them all), who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, once missed a man from among his companions. Then he saw him after a time, and said to him: "What has kept you from us so long?" He said: "Illness and poverty, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said to him: "Shall I not teach you supplications with which you would pray, and Allah would remove illness from you and drive poverty away from you?" He said to him: "Yes, may my parents be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah." So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: Say:

"There is no might nor power except by Allah. I entrust myself to the Ever-Living Who never dies. All praise be to Allah, Who has not taken a son, and Who has no partner in His Dominion, and Who has no protector out of weakness. And magnify Him with great glorification."

key_terms.السقم: Illness, sickness; a broad term for chronic or severe disease
key_terms.الفقر: Poverty, destitution; lack of material sustenance
key_terms.توكلت على الحي الذي لا يموت: I entrust myself to the Ever-Living Who never dies; an expression of absolute reliance on God
key_terms.لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله: There is no might nor power except by Allah; one of the greatest formulas of dhikr
key_terms.وكبره تكبيرا: And magnify Him with great glorification; from Quran 17:111

ai.seo_question: What supplication did the Prophet teach to ward off illness and poverty?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Amali of al-Mufid, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that the Prophet (PBUH) noticed a companion's prolonged absence. When the man returned and explained that illness and poverty had kept him away, the Prophet taught him a powerful supplication combining 'la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' (there is no might nor power except by Allah) with verses from the end of Surah al-Isra (17:111). This teaching reflects the early Muslim practice of seeking divine help through dhikr and Quranic recitation for both spiritual and material hardships.
